pharm: Long-acting proton pump inhibitor that irreversibly inhibits gastric H+/K+-ATPase to suppress acid secretion; used for acid-peptic disorders
quick: 10-20 mg once daily (duodenal ulcer typically 10 mg)
Before a meal, usually in the morning
Avoid unless clearly needed; limited data
Symptom response, Mg/B12 on long-term use
summary: Ilaprazole is a long-acting substituted-benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor that irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+-ATPase, providing prolonged suppression of gastric acid secretion. It is used for duodenal and gastric ulcers, reflux esophagitis and as part of Helicobacter pylori eradication regimens. Its long half-life and largely CYP3A4-mediated (rather than CYP2C9-dependent) metabolism reduce variability between CYP2C19 metabolizer phenotypes. It is approved in countries such as South Korea, China and India but is not FDA-approved in the United States; long-term PPI class precautions apply.

dosage.d: 10-20 mg twice daily with two antibiotics
dosage.n: Usually 7-14 days as part of a regimen

dosage.d: Use with caution; consider lower dose

admin: Take once daily, typically in the morning before food
Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew enteric-coated tablets
For H. pylori, take together with the prescribed antibiotics
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration needed
moa: A prodrug that accumulates in the acidic secretory canaliculi of gastric parietal cells, where it is converted to the active sulfenamide and covalently binds cysteine residues of the H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump), irreversibly inhibiting the final step of gastric acid secretion; its long duration of action gives sustained acid suppression.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to ilaprazole or other substituted benzimidazole PPIs
relative: Long-term/high-dose use (osteoporosis, hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency risk)
Concurrent drugs needing gastric acid for absorption

preg: Limited data; avoid in pregnancy unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: Limited data on excretion in breast milk; avoid or use with caution during breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is generally expected, as elimination is largely non-renal; use clinical judgement.
hepatic: Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment, where clearance may be reduced; consider a lower dose.

major: Rilpivirine - reduced absorption and antiviral efficacy (avoid)
Atazanavir / nelfinavir - markedly reduced antiretroviral levels
moderate: Drugs needing acid for absorption (ketoconazole, itraconazole, iron salts, erlotinib) - reduced absorption
interactions.food: Best taken before a meal; food may modestly affect absorption
interactions.alcohol: Limit; alcohol can aggravate gastric irritation
interactions.diagnostics: Suppressed acid can cause false-negative urea breath tests and elevated chromogranin A; can affect H. pylori testing

serious: Bone fractures with long-term high-dose use

monitoring: Renal function if interstitial nephritis suspected
counsel: Take once daily before food, usually in the morning
Swallow the tablet whole; do not crush or chew
Use for the shortest effective duration; report ongoing symptoms
Report persistent diarrhea, muscle cramps, palpitations or severe rash
Tell your doctor about HIV medicines and other drugs you take
Long-term use can affect magnesium, vitamin B12 and bone health
pk: Acid suppression within hours; full effect over a few days
~3.5-9 h (long for a PPI; prolonged acid suppression)
Acid suppression persists well beyond plasma half-life (>24 h)
Below 25-30 C, protect from light and moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved; approved in South Korea, China and India among others
Longer-acting than older PPIs, giving sustained acid suppression
Metabolism is less dependent on CYP2C19, reducing inter-patient variability
Apply PPI class cautions: hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency, fractures, C. difficile, interstitial nephritis
Avoid with rilpivirine and acid-dependent antiretrovirals; pending clinical review for FDA status
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Experience is limited; expect exaggerated pharmacologic effects with no specific syndrome. Management is symptomatic and supportive; ilaprazole is highly protein-bound and not readily dialyzable, and there is no specific antidote.
refs: FDA PPI class safety communications (hypomagnesemia, fractures, C. difficile)
